Summary, courtesy of Crunchyroll:
Succubi, dullahans, snow women and vampires... We're a little different from humans and called "demi-humans." Lately, we've been called "demis." My thoughts:

  • My initial apprehensions about this being subtle SJW bait were unfounded. Or rather, it approaches the concept of social justice with the correct view in mind, i.e. 1) you must bring something interesting to the table for me to give a shit about your welfare, and 2) women need a strong father/husband figure to keep them in line.

  • Tetsuo could have been fleshed out more, but he's more than a Gary Stu for the audience to project on to. Haters will say "wow he got a bunch of high school girls to fawn over him through the miracle of showing up" but 1) this totally happens IRL and 2) the author has storytelling talent but he's not getting paid to give a bunch of backstory to horny weebs looking for the next flavor-of-the-month jerkoff material

  • Hikari is daughterfu or friendfu material, but top notch at that. The world needs more HIGH ENERGY funny girls, and far far far less useless thots that think being a skanky piece of shit or a nonstop bad attitude is an acceptable substitute for personality. The series does a good job of subtly conveying that she's not ready for a romantic relationship, which was unexpected but welcome, in the sense that I don't think I've ever seen an anime where any girl over the age of 12 was not immediately ready to service your every sexual or romantic desire

  • Hikari's dad is the king cuck of rice island. Make memes of this nao plz

  • Machi (Kyoko? I don't know how these jap names work) is appealing, but like Tetsuo, suffers from a lack of backstory. The thing where she wants to joke about being a dullahan had so. much. potential. Like, hey wow, a girl whom'st eyes really are "down here." He shoots from the 3 point line, he scores. Boom goes the dynamite. How hard was that, Petos?

  • The thing with Tetsuo's physicist friend spazzing out over Machi seemed like an entirely unnecessary episode. TL;DR: instead of magic, maybe a wormhole connects a dullahan's head and body, yet the result is the same - nobody gives a shit

  • Yuki needs a rewrite to be more interesting, but I'm glad they took the premise of "shy snow woman" and didn't fill in the following blank space with "whomst has a dark past"

  • Sakie is nice. I hope her and Tetsuo hook up.

  • EXCEPT YOU'LL NEVER FUCKING FIND OUT BECAUSE THEY SHAT OUT THE MOST BULLSHIT ENDING EVER IN THE HISTORY OF ANYTHING. Spoiler alert: "yo fam I know school is out for the summer, so let's all go to the pool" / "a'ight assemble tha krew" / end credits. Christ

  • Episode 7 was entirely unnecessary. Look, I know why you're here, watching these things - you're vaguely upset with the direction your life has gone in that you're successful in an exoteric sense but haven't accomplished anything of meaning, work isn't fulfilling, you haven't really committed yourself to anything meaningful for the foreseeable future, you're technically never alone but you live in solitude, so you're pissing your days away watching harem animes and wishing you were old enough to collect social security and/or a fentanyl prescription - but look, the 23 minutes of life that episode 7 will let you fast forward through should really be filled by literally anything else. Much like your life, there is no story worth telling here, the difference being that I'm giving you a way out by telling you here and now that this episode is a complete waste of time.

  • For all my bitching, I found myself eagerly plowing through each episode (except 7, which I spent waiting for something interesting to happen, only to discover that the characters meticulously introduced would only be used for 2 throwaway gags for the rest of the series). I found myself vested in the characters, even the poorly written ones, and these are truly the most three dimensional 2D waifus I've ever had had the pleasure of seeing. The real tragedy isn't that the series was short and rushed, it's knowing that we missed out on something magical, all because some sushijews got cold feet after getting poor ratings because the cucks of rice island were too foolish to know what was set before them. Tibbets, get the nukes.

  • There was a surprising lack of fan service. The only thing that really stands out is Sakie donning a bikini at the end, but I get it - you can't really impress that a succubus has sex appeal without getting downright lewd

SUMMARY: Definitely recommend, but get ready for a little disappointment (or heartbreak, depending on how fucking pathetic you are)
